meta.tubeless_callout: TUBELESS TIRES ARE MANDATORY. Cactus spines will shred tubes on this route. Riders run 27.5×2.8 plus — in-spec and adequate. Run sealant fresh and carry plugs.
meta.water_callout: Per-rider water capacity for THIS loop is 4–6 L. Near-full bottles are only needed on the flagged dry stretches — the longest is ~34 mi / 54 km (Todos Santos → El Rosario). The big remote-desert water figures you'll read for the full Baja Divide are for sections that are NOT on the Cape Loop. Do not over-pack water for this route.
meta.season_note: January: warm days, cold nights at elevation. Sleep + layers must handle ~40°F / 5°C nights.

tiers.name: Tier 1 — Per-rider
tiers.subtitle: Each rider carries their own. Full redundancy by default — no single point of failure.

items.name: Sleep system (~40°F / 5°C)
items.detail: Bag/quilt + pad rated for cold nights at elevation.

items.name: Water capacity 4–6 L
items.detail: Bottles/bladder totaling 4–6 L. Carry near-full only on the four flagged dry stretches.

items.name: Personal first aid
items.detail: Blister care, meds, personal scripts, ibuprofen, electrolytes.

items.name: Cold-night layers
items.detail: Insulated jacket, warm hat, gloves, long layers for ~40°F nights.

items.name: Headlamp + spare batteries
items.detail: Camp + emergency night riding.

items.name: Nutrition
items.detail: Snacks/calories to cover the longest stretch between resupply.

items.name: Phone + charging
items.detail: Offline maps + this site downloaded. Cable + plug.

items.name: ID + cash (pesos)
items.detail: Passport, cash for towns without ATMs, card. ATMs only in the bigger towns.

items.name: Sun protection
items.detail: Sunscreen, lip balm, sun hoody/sleeves, sunglasses — desert sun is relentless.

items.name: Chemical water tabs
items.detail: Per-rider backup to the shared filter — everyone carries tabs.

tiers.name: Tier 2 — Shared-once
tiers.subtitle: One carrier for the whole group. SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE — if that rider bails, the group loses it. Assign carriers explicitly before departure.

items.name: Satellite communicator (inReach)
items.detail: At least one in the group — HIGHEST-PRIORITY shared item. No cell coverage on long stretches; this is the emergency lifeline. Strongly consider a second device for redundancy.

items.name: Stove + gasoline-compatible fuel
items.detail: Run a stove that burns gasoline — alcohol/canister fuel is hard to source in Baja per bikepacking.com. Refill gas in towns.

items.name: Pot / cook kit
items.detail: One pot for the group; pairs with the stove carrier.

items.name: Primary trauma kit
items.detail: Group-level trauma: tourniquet, pressure dressing, wound care — beyond personal first aid.

tiers.name: Tier 3 — Redundant-shared
tiers.subtitle: Carried by 2 of 3 riders so one rider bailing doesn't strip the group of a critical repair item.

items.name: Tubeless plug kit + spare sealant
items.detail: Plugs for cactus punctures + sealant to refresh/refill.

items.name: Pump (2×)
items.detail: Two pumps in the group — tubeless reseating needs volume.

items.name: Spare tubes
items.detail: Backup even on tubeless — for sidewall gashes plugs won't hold.

items.name: Chain links + chain tool
items.detail: Quick links + tool to fix a broken chain.

items.name: Derailleur hanger (per-rider, bike-specific)
items.detail: Hangers are frame-specific — EACH rider carries their own. Listed here because a bent hanger is a trip-ender otherwise.

items.name: Multitool
items.detail: Hex/torx + driver set.

items.name: Brake pads
items.detail: Spare pads — long sandy descents eat them.

items.name: Spokes + spare cable
items.detail: Spoke wrench, a few spokes, a shift/brake cable.

items.name: Voile straps
items.detail: Field fixes for racks, loads, splints — endlessly useful.

items.name: Zip ties + tape
items.detail: Gorilla/electrical tape + assorted zip ties.

items.name: Water filter
items.detail: One filter for the group (everyone also carries chemical tabs as Tier-1 backup).
